steps.description:
In games, nothing excites a programmer more than coding an opponent clever enough to beat them at their own creation. Though sometimes, crafting a wildly lucky adversary is just as thrilling.

You are coding your own Scissors Paper Stone game that can compete with you!

     

You know the game best. Let's start with the program breakdown.

Observe the sample game play and fill in the blanks of the flow diagram using 3 Comment blocks.

You are coding your own Scissors Paper Stone game that can compete with you!

              

Load up your previous step with the 3 Comment blocks. Compare them with a suggested guide below.

In this step, we will focus on the FIRST PART: "Display & Input Options".

Create the code to display as shown in the diagram. When the player hits one of the buttons, the program clears the screen and ends.

     

Repeat While/Until loop and OR operators may help.

A variable can be assigned a number or text.
  

You can use the Random block to generate a number, perfect for making unpredictable choices in your game or activity.

Load up your previous code where you have implemented the first part on "Display & Input Options".

In this step, we will focus on the SECOND PART: "Display Choice".

Upon a button press, display the player's choice (scissors, paper or stone) and a random Bot choice.

A variable can be assigned a number or text.
  

You can use the Random block to generate a number, perfect for making unpredictable choices in your game or activity.

Load up your previous code where you have implemented the first two parts on "Display & Input Options" and "Display Choice".

In this step, we will implement the THIRD PART: "Show Result". 

The table below shows the possible results. The program will show the "win" beside the winner or "tie" at the top-right corner. The game will repeat after the result is shown for 3 seconds.
